title: Branch Gave Its Terrific Office Chair a Gaming Makeover, and I Am All for It
author: Louryn Strampe
text: $569 at BranchAll products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, when you buy something through our retail links, we may earn an affiliate commission.Rating:8/10WIREDComfortable. Ventilated. Supremely adjustable. Painless (mostly) assembly.TIREDHard to dial in the right position at first. Subpar headrest if you're short. A little scared to get Hot Cheetos dust on white leather.There aren’t many differences between what you’d need for a good office chair versus a good gaming chair, but for some reason, they’re often marketed differently. And that’s usually what separates them: marketing. When Branch released variations of the WIRED-favorite Ergonomic Chair Pro in collaboration with Sega, I was stoked to try it from a gamer perspective for our buying guide rather than from an office warrior POV. It checks every box: It has the comfortable ergonomics you'd expect from an adjustable office chair, with the subtle, pleasing designs inspired by one of gaming's most revered companies.Looks GoodPhotograph: Louryn StrampeThis Sega collaboration comes in three aesthetically pleasing designs that pay homage to the company's icons. The Sonic version has a mesh back, while the Genesis and Dreamcast versions have vegan leather instead. I tested the Dreamcast version, and I love the way it looks. It has iconic wheel designs inspired by the controller, plus a slick orange stripe on the armrests that harkens back to the console's swirly logo.Assembling furniture continues to be one of the most frustrating parts of reviewing gear, but I aim to do it the same exact way a WIRED reader might: by myself with copious amounts of swearing. In this case, the experience actually wasn’t that bad. The box it ships in should be lifted by two people, unless you're like me, who goes to the gym and lives alone with a cat. I managed all 50-ish pounds up the stairs and assembled it in about an hour. I especially liked the labeled bolt packaging, and the included Allen key, which was sturdy and much better than you’d typically find in a furniture package. Instructions weren’t too difficult, nor were any of the pieces particularly cumbersome.I am slightly concerned that my Dreamcast version is a white gaming chair, while the other two designs are darker. I wear a lot of dark clothing and eat a slightly above-average amount of spicy chips, so staining and ease of cleaning will be two things I look for during long-term testing. In the meantime, I will just cross my fingers that my cat doesn’t take too much of a liking to it and that I don't absentmindedly drop too many Cheetos crumbs.Feels BetterThere’s a bit of a learning curve when adjusting the ergonomics. With 14 adjustment points, from lumbar support to seat tilt and depth to multiple armrest planes, it can be painstaking to dial everything in just right. But once you figure out the knobs and levers, it’s beyond easy to lock in a position to game (or work) for hours at a time. The included headrest wasn’t perfect for me—though it is adjustable, it doesn’t lower or move forward enough for my 5’ 1” frame. Otherwise, I stayed very comfortable in this chair. The Ergonomic Pro is compatible with Branch’s tall cylinder, which you may want if you’re 5’ 11” or taller.Photograph: Louryn StrampeAlthough the difference between these and the non-Sega edition is mainly looks, it still feels more like a gaming chair than the office variant (note that the Sega chairs include the otherwise optional headrest). It doesn’t go so far as to emulate a race car seat, which so many gaming chairs do (poorly), but it kept me comfortable over hours-long gaming sessions. The seat cushioning is plenty plush, and the casters are smooth when I’m rolling around my apartment.Overall, I’m impressed by this chair, which offers office-level ergonomics with gamer appeal. The price isn’t eye-watering, especially when compared to other chairs that I’ve tested and liked less. The design isn’t so over-the-top that your office will look like a Twitch streamer’s game cave. If you want the best of both worlds, this is the right chair for you.Power up with unlimited access to WIRED.
